content.text:
Nucleum, Memotron, and Pointron share one component chain. Each app is a thin SvelteKit host; product identity is injected at `apps/<product>/src/local.ts`, and every screen after that is resolved from the shared route tree in `client/routes`.

## Starting points

| App | Product assembly | Product shell |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nucleum | `apps/nucleus/src/local.ts` | `NucleusBaseLayer` |
| Pointron | `apps/pointron/src/local.ts` | `PointronBaseLayer` |
| Memotron | `apps/memotron/src/local.ts` | `MemotronBaseLayer` |

Each `local.ts` spreads that product's config and sets `base` to the product layer. SvelteKit routes live in `client/routes` (`apps/nucleus/svelte.config.js` aliases `routes` there). Timear is outside this chain: it has its own routes under `apps/timear/src/routes` and a layout that only renders `children`.

The file that inverts dependencies is `client/composition/configure-hosts.ts`. It is imported by `BaseLayer` before any screen renders, and it installs the hosts lower layers call (action renderer, product config, overlay, shortcuts, record renderer, surface config) so shell, features, and UI never import composition.

## Component chain

Authenticated app routes (`client/routes/(app)/[...route]/+page.svelte` and `.../tab/+page.svelte`) all mount `PagePainterV2`. Account routes (`client/routes/account`) stop earlier, at `AccountLayout`.

```
app.html
└─ client/routes/+layout.svelte
   └─ BaseLayer                          boot: session, launch context, commands, service worker
      ├─ MetadataLayer
      └─ ThemeLayer
         └─ client/routes/(app)/+layout.svelte
            └─ AuthGuard                 plan gate, bootstrap redirect, extension login
               └─ productData.base       Nucleus | Pointron | Memotron BaseLayer
                  └─ UserBaseLayer       DataFn init, legacy recovery, loading gate
                     └─ UserLayout
                        └─ NavigationLayout          shell
                           ├─ WiredLeftNav / WiredTopNav   composition chrome snippets
                           └─ PagePainterV2
                              └─ ComponentResolver    path → action.component
                     ModalLayer, ShortcutRunner, Intercom
```

`BaseLayer` does the shared boot, in this order: app version, `accountSession.init()`, launch context, command registry (`global-commands` plus the product's actions), service worker, environment-change check, then connectivity. `UserBaseLayer` does not render the shell until both `isBaseLoaded` and `isLocalLoaded` are set; until then it shows `AppLoadingView` or the legacy recovery gate.

`PagePainterV2` turns the URL into an action via `appStore.resolveComponentFromPath`. The action renderer host, registered in `configure-hosts.ts`, is `ComponentResolver`, which renders that action's Svelte component. Shell chrome (panels, modals, portrait nav, resource pages) uses the same resolver. Product-specific chrome (logo, capture, focus widget, notifications) is supplied as snippets from the product base layer and the chrome adapters in `client/composition/chrome/`, not imported by the shell.

## Dependency map

`tools/check/client-dependency-matrix.json` is the enforced direct-import matrix (`npm run check:architecture`). One valid top-to-bottom order:

```
extensions, routes
    → composition
        → products
            → surfaces
                → features
                    → shell
                        → shared-state
                            → datafn → runtime → persistence
                            → config → next → ui → theme
```

Who may import whom:

| Owner | May import |
| --- | --- |
| `routes` | composition, products, surfaces, shell, shared-state, datafn, persistence, runtime, config, ui |
| `composition` | products, surfaces, features, shell, shared-state, datafn, persistence, runtime, config, ui, static |
| `products` | surfaces, features, shell, shared-state, datafn, runtime, config, next, ui |
| `surfaces` | features, shell, shared-state, datafn, persistence, runtime, config, next, theme, ui |
| `features` | shell, shared-state, datafn, persistence, runtime, config, theme, ui |
| `shell` | shared-state, datafn, runtime, config, theme, ui |
| `shared-state` | datafn, persistence, runtime, config, theme, ui |
| `datafn` | runtime, persistence, config, next |
| `runtime` | persistence |
| `ui` | theme |

`persistence`, `theme`, and `static` import no other client owner. Features never import surfaces, products, or composition. Shell never imports composition, surfaces, or products; product nav arrives only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`, and brand, search, bulk edit, offline status, and profile arrive as snippets from `client/composition/chrome/`.

# Client dependency map

Readable view of the post-reorganization client graph and the Nucleum, Memotron, and Pointron component chain.

The enforced direct-import list is `tools/check/client-dependency-matrix.json`. `npm run check:architecture` rejects imports outside that matrix, including type-only imports. Ownership rules and historical notes live in [client boundaries](client-boundaries.md).

Arrows in the owner diagram mean "may import". An owner may also import its own files. The diagram is one valid top-to-bottom order, not every permitted edge. The matrix table below is the full direct-import list.

## Owner order

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  extensions["extensions"]
  routes["routes"]
  composition["composition"]
  products["products"]
  surfaces["surfaces"]
  features["features"]
  shell["shell"]
  sharedState["shared-state"]
  datafn["datafn"]
  runtime["runtime"]
  persistence["persistence"]
  config["config"]
  next["next"]
  ui["ui"]
  theme["theme"]

  extensions --> composition
  routes --> composition
  composition --> products
  products --> surfaces
  surfaces --> features
  features --> shell
  shell --> sharedState
  sharedState --> datafn
  datafn --> runtime
  runtime --> persistence
  datafn --> config
  config --> next
  next --> ui
  ui --> theme
```

`apps/` entrypoints may assemble composition and products. Product source cannot import composition. `persistence`, `theme`, `static`, `ambient`, `app.css`, and `svelte.config.mjs` import no other client owner.

## Direct imports

| Importing owner | May import |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions` | `app.css`, `composition`, `config`, `datafn`, `features`, `persistence`, `runtime`, `shared-state`, `shell`, `surfaces`, `ui` |
| `routes` | `app.css`, `composition`, `config`, `datafn`, `persistence`, `products`, `runtime`, `shared-state`, `shell`, `surfaces`, `ui` |
| `composition` | `config`, `datafn`, `features`, `persistence`, `products`, `runtime`, `shared-state`, `shell`, `static`, `surfaces`, `ui` |
| `products` | `config`, `datafn`, `features`, `next`, `runtime`, `shared-state`, `shell`, `surfaces`, `ui` |
| `surfaces` | `config`, `datafn`, `features`, `next`, `persistence`, `runtime`, `shared-state`, `shell`, `theme`, `ui` |
| `features` | `config`, `datafn`, `persistence`, `runtime`, `shared-state`, `shell`, `theme`, `ui` |
| `shell` | `config`, `datafn`, `runtime`, `shared-state`, `theme`, `ui` |
| `shared-state` | `config`, `datafn`, `persistence`, `runtime`, `theme`, `ui` |
| `datafn` | `config`, `next`, `persistence`, `runtime` |
| `runtime` | `persistence` |
| `config` | `next` |
| `next` | `ui` |
| `ui` | `theme` |

Inside `client/ui`, compositions may use elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts. Those lower layers cannot import compositions.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  compositions["ui/compositions"]
  elements["ui/elements"]
  actions["ui/actions"]
  icons["ui/icons"]
  illustrations["ui/illustrations"]
  branding["ui/branding"]
  environment["ui/environment"]
  hosts["ui/hosts"]
  theme["theme"]

  compositions --> elements
  compositions --> actions
  compositions --> icons
  compositions --> illustrations
  compositions --> branding
  compositions --> environment
  compositions --> hosts
  elements --> theme
  actions --> theme
  icons --> theme
  illustrations --> theme
  branding --> theme
  environment --> theme
  hosts --> theme
```

Edges that stay closed:

- Features do not import products, surfaces, or composition. Shell is the only app-level layer they may use.
- Shell does not import composition, surfaces, or products.
- Surfaces do not import composition.
- Shared-state does not import composition, features, or products.
- DataFn and runtime do not import features, products, composition, shell, UI, or shared-state.
- UI does not import application state, runtime, shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state.

## Host inversion

Lower layers do not import composition to reach product behavior. `client/composition/configure-hosts.ts` runs from `BaseLayer` and installs narrow hosts. Shell, features, surfaces, and UI call those hosts.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  configureHosts["configure-hosts.ts"]
  sharedHosts["shared-state hosts"]
  uiHosts["ui/hosts and ui/environment"]
  shell["shell"]
  features["features"]
  surfaces["surfaces"]
  ui["ui"]

  configureHosts --> sharedHosts
  configureHosts --> uiHosts
  shell --> sharedHosts
  features --> sharedHosts
  surfaces --> sharedHosts
  ui --> uiHosts
```

Product navigation reaches the shell only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`. Brand, search, bulk edit, offline status, capture, and profile reach shell chrome as snippets from `client/composition/chrome/`. Persistence receives its logger through `persistence/logging-host`.

## App component chain

Nucleum, Memotron, and Pointron are thin SvelteKit hosts. Each app points its routes at `client/routes`. Product identity is `apps/<product>/src/local.ts`, which sets `base` to that product's layer.

| App | Assembly | Product layer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nucleum | `apps/nucleus/src/local.ts` | `NucleusBaseLayer` |
| Pointron | `apps/pointron/src/local.ts` | `PointronBaseLayer` |
| Memotron | `apps/memotron/src/local.ts` | `MemotronBaseLayer` |

Timear does not use this chain. Its routes live under `apps/timear/src/routes`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  rootLayout["routes/+layout.svelte"]
  baseLayer["BaseLayer"]
  themeLayer["ThemeLayer"]
  appGroup["routes/(app)/+layout.svelte"]
  authGuard["AuthGuard"]
  productBase["productData.base"]
  userBase["UserBaseLayer"]
  userLayout["UserLayout"]
  navLayout["NavigationLayout"]
  chrome["WiredLeftNav and WiredTopNav"]
  painter["PagePainterV2"]
  resolver["ComponentResolver"]
  accountLayout["AccountLayout"]

  rootLayout --> baseLayer --> themeLayer
  themeLayer --> appGroup --> authGuard --> productBase
  productBase --> userBase --> userLayout --> navLayout
  navLayout --> chrome
  navLayout --> painter --> resolver
  themeLayer --> accountLayout
```

`BaseLayer` boots the shared app: version, account session, launch context, command registry, service worker, then connectivity. `configure-hosts.ts` is imported before children render.

`AuthGuard` checks the product plan, sends an unbootstrapped cloud user to `/bootstrap`, and completes extension login. It then mounts `productData.base`.

`UserBaseLayer` initializes DataFn and legacy recovery. It renders `UserLayout` only after `isBaseLoaded` and `isLocalLoaded`. Until then it shows `AppLoadingView` or the recovery gate. After load it also mounts `ModalLayer`, `ShortcutRunner`, and Intercom.

`NavigationLayout` is the shell: left nav, top nav, split view, right panel, bottom nav, and trail. `PagePainterV2` maps the URL to an action. The action-renderer host is `ComponentResolver`, which renders that action's component. Panels, modals, and resource pages use the same resolver.

Account routes (`client/routes/account`) stop at `AccountLayout` from `client/surfaces/account`. They do not mount the product base layer.

# Client ownership and import boundaries

Current ownership contract for the client. If this file disagrees with `tools/check/client-dependency-matrix.json` or `npm run check:architecture`, the checker wins. Update this file in the same change that moves an owner or an allowed edge.

Diagrams and the direct-import matrix live in [client dependency map](client-dependency-map.md). Type placement lives in [type ownership](type-ownership.md). The TIDY-477 phase journal lives in [history/tidy-477-client-boundaries.md](history/tidy-477-client-boundaries.md).

## Ownership

| Owner | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` | Resource definitions, cross-layer product identity (`schema/product.type.ts`), and billing wire contracts (`schema/account`). |
| `client/config` | Client product identity, action identifiers, and declarative navigation metadata. |
| `client/datafn` | Client storage, the sync runtime, visibility sync, and the live DataFn client in `datafn.store.ts`. |
| `client/runtime` | Account transport and session state, network authority, connectivity, logging, browser and embed context, service-worker registration, native messages, inference, and telemetry SDK mechanics. |
| `client/persistence` | Client storage, device identity, legacy local storage, migrations, and legacy backup. The logger arrives through `persistence/logging-host`. |
| `client/ui` | Domain-free portable presentation (`@21n/ui`). See the UI layers below. |
| `client/shared-state` | Product-independent client behavior under the named owners below. No root barrel. |
| `client/shell` | Navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, connected notification rendering, and global shortcut execution (`@nucleum/shell`). |
| `client/features` | Capability implementations. Memory owns Markdown editing and tags. Spaces owns combinations. Records owns connected record menus and bulk mutations. Focus owns its scheduled notification queue. |
| `client/surfaces` | Cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface, search, and library (`@nucleum/surfaces`). |
| `client/products` | Product experiences composed from those capabilities. Product source does not import composition. |
| `client/composition` | The composition root, `layers/`, and `chrome/`: host installation, base and user layers, command-registry assembly, and product-aware branding adapters (`@nucleum/composition`). |
| `client/routes` | The shared SvelteKit route tree for Nucleum, Memotron, and Pointron. |
| `apps/` | Thin product hosts. `apps/<product>/src/local.ts` selects that product's base layer. Timear keeps its own routes. |

`client/ui` layers:

| Layer | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `elements` | Atomic controls and UI-only types. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `elements/keyboard`. |
| `compositions` | Domain-neutral compound UI, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. |
| `actions` | Generic DOM behavior. Capability-specific actions stay beside their consumer. |
| `icons`, `illustrations`, `branding` | Portable icons, artwork, and pure visual marks. |
| `environment` | Portable viewport and presentation measurements. |
| `hosts` | Dependency-inversion contracts shared by controls and compositions. |

`client/shared-state` owners: `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, `shortcuts`. Import a named subpath such as `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`.

State that looks shared but has a narrower owner:

| Concern | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Browser and embed environment | `client/runtime/context.store.ts` |
| Account session state | `client/runtime/account/account.store.ts` |
| Sign-in, sign-out, bootstrap, and DataFn teardown | `client/surfaces/account/account-session.ts` |
| Account deletion | `client/surfaces/account/account-deletion.ts` |
| Subscription operations | `client/surfaces/subscription` |
| File upload, conversion, and storage | `client/shared-state/files` |
| URL and resource navigation | `client/shell/navigation/navigation.ts` |
| Command lookup and execution | `client/surfaces/commands/action-runner.ts` |
| Command definitions | The feature, surface, shell, or product that owns the action. `client/composition/global-commands.ts` only preserves assembly order. |
| Headless notifications | `client/shared-state/notifications` |
| Connected notification rendering | `client/shell/notifications` |
| Shortcut persistence and matching | `client/shared-state/shortcuts` |
| Global shortcut execution | `client/shell/shortcuts` |
| Shortcut settings | `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts` |
| Selection state and the resource-action host | `client/shared-state/resources` |
| Support integration | `client/surfaces/help/support`, mounted by composition |
| Diagnostics and error screens | `client/surfaces/help` |
| Legacy recovery presentation | `client/surfaces/settings/data-recovery` |

## Closed edges

`npm run check:architecture` enforces the matrix in `tools/check/client-dependency-matrix.json`, including type-only imports. These are the edges that are easy to miss from the matrix alone:

- Features do not import products, surfaces, or composition. Shell is the only app-level layer they may use. Surfaces may compose features.
- Surfaces do not import composition. Product fields arrive through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/surface-config-host`.
- Shell does not import composition, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation arrives through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`.
- Shared-state does not import composition, features, or products, directly or transitively, including through type-only imports.
- DataFn and runtime do not import features, products, composition, shell, UI, or shared-state.
- UI does not import application state, runtime, shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state, directly or transitively.
- Inside UI, compositions may use elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts. Those lower layers do not import compositions.
- Composition calculations do not import the session singleton.
- A caller outside a capability uses a source file listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`. That list is the public surface, not a barrel. Additions are an explicit contract change. Package exports expose the same paths.

Tests and stories are outside the production-source import gate. `client/ui` is one matrix owner; the lower-layer rule above is separate. The aggregate `client/package.json` is not a matrix owner.

## Hosts

Lower layers do not import composition to reach product behavior. `client/composition/configure-hosts.ts` runs from the base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution.

| Contract | Installed by | Read by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Action renderer, overlay, resource action, resource panel, record renderer, recents, and shortcut hosts | `configure-hosts.ts` | Shell, features, and surfaces |
| `@21n/ui/hosts` and `@21n/ui/environment` | `configure-hosts.ts`, or the owning shell or feature adapter | Portable UI |
| `product-config-host` | Composition | Shell |
| `surface-config-host` | Composition | Surfaces |
| Chrome snippets (brand, search, bulk edit, offline status, capture, profile) | `client/composition/chrome/` | Shell, through optional snippet props |
| `persistence/logging-host` | Composition | Persistence |

Shell and feature adapters pass view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Do not add a compatibility wrapper or a generic service locator.

## Placement rules

These rules are semantic. The import checker does not decide them.

- A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. Keep a domain-neutral composition in `client/ui/compositions` when future reuse is intentional.
- A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` turns resource and path metadata into those items. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails stay in the shell while they own URL state, resource resolution, or product menus.
- Product-aware branding that reads persistence or account identity stays in a named composition adapter, such as `client/composition/SubAtomLogo.svelte`, and composes portable marks through props.
- Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing. Memory owns Markdown editing.
- Account runtime state does not own file processing, deletion confirmation, or subscription workflows.
- Do not recreate `client/utils`, `client/stores`, `client/state`, `client/commands`, `client/events`, `client/layout`, `client/branding`, `client/illustrations`, `client/icons`, `client/iconsV2`, or `client/application`. Do not add a catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory.
- When moving a module, update callers, feature exports, dependency declarations, and type-inventory destinations directly. Do not leave a compatibility re-export.

# Type and contract ownership

Current type-placement contract. If this file disagrees with `docs/architecture/type-ownership-inventory.json` or `node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs`, the checker wins. Update the inventory in the same change that moves a type module.

Application, navigation, account, file, and command ownership lives in [client boundaries](client-boundaries.md). The TIDY-478 phase journal lives in [history/tidy-478-type-ownership.md](history/tidy-478-type-ownership.md).

## Conventions

Definitions stay beside their implementation unless independent consumers need a neutral contract. Feature contracts belong to the feature, and external callers use the public entries in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`.

Portable UI controls own their structural prop and style types:

| Contract | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Primitive prop and style types | `client/ui/elements` |
| Domain-neutral composition contracts | `client/ui/compositions` |
| Generic DOM-action contracts | `client/ui/actions` |
| Package-wide host contracts | `client/ui/hosts` |
| Portable platform state | `client/ui/environment` |
| Visual asset contracts | `client/ui/icons`, `client/ui/illustrations`, or `client/ui/branding` |

Those UI contracts do not derive from schema records, DataFn resources, runtime types, application actions, or state interfaces. Owning adapters translate domain models at the UI boundary.

| Contract | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Keyboard and interaction mode | `client/ui/elements/keyboard` |
| Application action identifiers | `client/config` |
| Command host | `client/shared-state/commands` |
| Application events | `client/shared-state/events`. Focus and memory events live here. Clipper transport events live in `client/runtime/extensions`. |
| Resource panel and selection | `client/shared-state/resources` |
| Headless notification state | `client/shared-state/notifications` |
| Connected notification rendering | `client/shell/notifications` |
| Error recovery screens | `client/surfaces/help/errors` |
| Product menu contracts | `client/shell/navigation/app-menu.type.ts` |
| Browser ambient declarations | `client/ambient` |
| Cross-layer account, subscription, and legacy wire contracts | `schema` |
| Generated AuthFn and DataFn/Drizzle files | `services/account` generation scripts. Do not edit them by hand. |

`schema/account` owns profile and subscription wire data. Billing presentation fields stay in `client/surfaces/subscription`. `schema/legacy` owns the existing Surreal mutation, query, sync, resource-action, and store-data encodings. Do not derive those legacy shapes from current DataFn records. `schema/datafn.ts` derives resource names from `nucleumDatafnSchema`. Client `Resource`, `MetaResource`, and `Product` compose schema values with the Next overlay; backend callers import schema directly.

Generic error codes are schema-owned. The default error message belongs to `client/shared-state/notifications`. Markdown validation belongs to memory. Responsive text truncation belongs to the text primitive. The legacy relay request contract lives in `server/common/relay/relay.type.ts` and imports only schema-owned resource and query contracts.

Native transcription model identifiers and worker model identifiers are different protocols. Both live in `client/runtime/inference`, in separate modules, with their original enum values.

The global `client/types` and `shared/types` packages are retired. Do not replace them with a catch-all types package or a compatibility export. Splits use a direct import to the actual owner.

## Import and export rules

Import interfaces and aliases with `import type` or a named `type` specifier. A runtime enum stays a value import. Do not re-export a moved definition from its former location. Public feature entries in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json` match the feature package exports. DataFn and schema expose their contracts directly.

`npm run check:architecture` checks static imports, exports, dynamic imports, import types, CommonJS requires, and Vitest mock imports. It rejects production schema, shared, server, and service imports into client code, rejects every server-to-client import, and rejects retired package aliases. Historical specs and append-only `.conduct` reports may still name the old layout. Active guidance and configuration use the current owners.

`node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs` checks every recorded destination in [type-ownership-inventory.json](type-ownership-inventory.json) and compares runtime enum declarations to that baseline. One audited retirement is recorded there: the disconnected shell cache `CacheKey` enum. No other runtime-enum retirement is exempt.

The architecture docs now separate the current contract from the phase journals.

**Current contracts**

- `docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md` is an ownership table, the closed edges, the host contracts, and the placement rules the import checker cannot decide.
- `docs/architecture/type-ownership.md` is the type-placement rules and the pointer to `type-ownership-inventory.json`. The checker still reads that JSON in place.
- `docs/architecture/client-dependency-map.md` remains the diagrams and the direct-import matrix.

Each current file says the checker wins if the prose drifts, and that the doc is updated in the same change as a move.

**Archives**

- `docs/architecture/history/tidy-477-client-boundaries.md` keeps the delivery checklist, follow-ups, and verification records.
- `docs/architecture/history/tidy-478-type-ownership.md` keeps the type-ownership checklist, audit narrative, and verification counts.

`AGENTS.md` now points agents at those current files and at `docs/architecture/history/` for the journals. That citation change is constitution 1.11.3, with no principle or workflow change.
